challenge.method: Test a case-only variant of a word-symbol and an identifier that adds a digit to that word-symbol.
challenge.results: Changing capitalization preserves the spelling, so the exclusion still applies. Adding a digit changes the spelling. Sharing a word-symbol prefix alone does not trigger the exclusion. Both results follow from applying the two sentences together.

limitations: The rule concerns identifier spelling, independent of case in the contents of character strings or extensions in later dialects.
The verification applies to ISO/IEC 7185:1990 lexical identifiers. Clause 6.1.3 does not govern the contents of string literals.
